title: Sight loss
summary: Woman in her thirties, living with her partner, certified severely sight impaired from retinitis pigmentosa. She reads only short items slowly with an electronic magnifier, cannot cook safely alone after a burn and a cut, labels her eye drops by touch, and needs a person or her guide dog for unfamiliar routes. Her partner reading the bills is a reading issue, not a budgeting one, and her difficulty in groups is visual, not an engagement need.
exercises: reading: aid vs cannot read at all
journeys: assistance dog / another person for unfamiliar routes
eye drops are medication, not therapy
aid mentioned without frequency or reliability (null draft)
misattribution: reading vs budgeting, sight vs engaging

conditions_in_documents: Retinitis pigmentosa, both eyes (severely sight impaired)
Healed fracture of right fifth metatarsal

must_find.quote: I don't use the hob much since I burnt myself.
Since then doesn't use oven or hob alone.
Cut finger peeling veg earlier this year, "steri-strips", now doesn't use the sharp knife.
Partner cooks evening meal every day.
Help needed with: reading print, getting around in unfamiliar places, using cooker safely

gaps: Form says 'don't use the hob much', notes say not alone at all; the difference should be noted
No kitchen review since her sight worsened
Whether she could cook a simple meal with supervision rather than having it cooked for her
activities.draft_note: She cannot cook safely without another person after a burn and a cut; the microwave and liquid level indicator do not cover preparing fresh food.

must_find.quote: I'm fine. Sometimes I knock my drink over.

gaps: Whether she can find food on the plate and cut it up without help
How often she spills or knocks things over
activities.draft_note: Only a passing mention of spills; nothing yet supports a scoring descriptor.

must_find.quote: She mentioned that the two drop bottles feel similar and she has on occasion used the wrong one.
stopping them is likely to allow the macular oedema to worsen.
Client now feels the label on each bottle every time before putting drops in.
I do my eye drops myself.

gaps: Tactile labels have been in use for only about 3 weeks
Who replaces the labels on new bottles (partner applied the first set)
activities.draft_note: Eye drops are medication, not therapy, so 3c to 3f do not apply; she needs an aid (tactile labels) to take them safely, and stopping them risks deterioration.
Form and notes both say no issues.
Form and notes both say no issues.

must_find.quote: Has a colour detector from rehab worker; client mentioned it in passing, adviser didn't ask how often she uses it or whether it works.
Rehabilitation worker issued talking colour detector and tactile bump-ons.
My partner sometimes tells me if something doesn't go or if I've got a mark on my top.
Didn't say how often.

gaps: How often she uses the colour detector, and whether she needs it to choose clothes
How often her partner points out stains or clashing clothes (a 2-week log has been requested)
Whether she would go out with stained or unsuitable clothing without that help
activities.draft_note: An aid (colour detector) and some prompting are mentioned, with no frequency or reliability; 6b or 6c(ii) cannot be chosen yet.

must_find.quote: I can't read letters or anything printed. I can't read signs when I'm out.
Uses electronic magnifier at home for short things like a label or an appointment date
Tried a letter from the council with it: "gave up after a couple of lines".
Near vision: N18 with her x6 electronic magnifier at close range, reading slowly. Unable to read N48 unaided.
Partner reads all post and bills to her, every week.

gaps: Whether reading even short items with the magnifier takes more than twice as long as normal
Whether the text-to-speech app counts as an aid that lets her read complex information reliably (notes say it gets lots wrong)
activities.draft_note: She reads basic information only with a magnifier, so 8e (cannot read at all) is not supported; expert to consider whether she cannot reliably read complex information even with aids.

must_find.quote: It's harder in a group because I can't see who is talking to me.
Fine one to one. Group situations at work harder, can't see faces or who's speaking, misses cues. No anxiety.

activities.draft_note: Difficulty in groups comes from sight, not a need for prompting or social support; she is fine one to one.

must_find.quote: My partner reads me the bills but I decide what we pay and when.
No difficulty with the decisions themselves, issue is reading the paperwork.

activities.draft_note: She makes the budgeting decisions herself; needing bills read out belongs under reading (activity 8).

must_find.quote: If it's somewhere new I need my partner or a friend to come with me
New places: needs partner or friend to go with her, or someone walks the route with her and the dog first.
Has got lost once trying a new route alone with cane
Long cane used outdoors "nearly always".
says only to partner's mum two doors along, "I just follow the wall".

gaps: Whether she can follow any familiar route other than two doors along without the cane or dog (relevant to 11f)
No clinical statement that the cane is needed on familiar routes; adviser has this on the to-do list
activities.draft_note: She needs another person or her guide dog (an assistance dog) to follow an unfamiliar route; 11f depends on more evidence about familiar routes without her cane.
No physical difficulty walking; the foot fracture has healed.

must_not_claim: That she reads Braille or that Braille is relevant to activity 8
That she has no light perception or total loss of vision
That she has anxiety or other mental health difficulty affecting journeys or engaging with people
That her partner manages her money or makes budgeting decisions for her
That she uses the colour detector daily or needs help to dress every day
That the eye drops count as therapy taking a set number of hours a week
